prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: The construction of / the new business school / is led to / a sudden rise of population in our area.
options: a sudden rise of population in our area
explanation: The construction actively caused the rise, so the passive 'is led to' is wrong; use the present perfect active 'has led to'.

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: What would / happen if / human beings were / governing by robots?
explanation: After 'were', the passive requires the past participle, so 'governing by robots' must become 'governed by robots'.

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: My friends are gone on a trip to Goa today.
explanation: 'Are gone' wrongly uses 'be' with an intransitive verb of movement; the present perfect 'have gone' is required.

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: One of the students is always / late to the class; he has warned / by the teacher many times; / but still, he keeps on being late.
options: One of the students is always
but still, he keeps on being late
late to the class; he has warned
explanation: The student receives the warning, so the passive is needed: 'he has been warned by the teacher', not 'he has warned'.

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: The man who / was committed / the theft last night / was caught this evening.
explanation: The man performed the theft, so the active past tense 'committed' is required instead of the passive 'was committed'.

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: He was unable / to help me because / he had been failed / to arrange the money.
explanation: 'Fail' is intransitive and cannot be passive here; it should be 'he had failed to arrange the money'.

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: Electric heaters were providing to all the officers at the guest house.
explanation: The heaters received the action, so the passive past participle is needed: 'were provided to all the officers'.

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: I think someone has been picked my pocket while I was travelling in the metro.
options: someone has been picked my pocket
explanation: 'Has been picked' is passive yet takes the object 'my pocket'; the active 'someone has picked my pocket' is correct.

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: Bags and purses were thoroughly checking at the entrance to the theatre.
explanation: Bags and purses are the receivers of the checking, so the passive 'were thoroughly checked' is required, not the continuous active form.

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: The children were warning / not to try / to climb the cliffs / as they were very steep.

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: My tailor is made / some very stylish dresses / for me as well as / for my daughter.

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: Despite warnings / the driver continued to speed / and has caught / by the traffic police.

sentence: She managed the company / so well that it is made / a huge profit that year.

both duration and quality of sleep.
